2.text: and wide enough for a person to walk about. The usual dimensions are

3.text: about 4½ feet in height, 7 feet in breadth, and 12 feet in length. The entrance
3.note: Printed as ‘4½’ (vulgar fraction one half, stacked numerator/denominator in the type). Also: a stray dot/period sits between ‘and’ and ‘12’ in the print (‘and.12’ at 2x); read as a punctuation blot per §2.14 (a mark of punctuation, not a letter or word, is keyed as nothing) rather than as an intended full stop — there is no sense in which a full stop belongs there.

4.text: is in the long side, which faces the flap of the outer tent.

5.text: The cover of the inner room is held in position by numerous loops

6.text: which are sewed to it, and are passed over two long horizontal poles. The

7.text: rear pole is fastened to the frame of the outer tent. The front pole is sup-

8.text: ported by two forked stakes of sufficient size. These stakes are called “thumbs”

9.text: (eˊtti). The floor is covered with willow twigs or with a coarse matting (Fig. 94)
9.resolved: eˊtti = e, U+02CA (word stress), t, t, i — gloss ‘thumbs’, glossed native (Chukchee) word for the forked support stakes
9.note: Raised mark between e and t defaults to stress U+02CA per keying_spec §4/§5.8 (‘read every raised mark as stress by default’); not U+0027 spirant/pause, neither of which has ever been the correct call.

27.text: of which the cover of the inner room is made varies considerably, according

28.text: to the season. In the cold season, while the family is still moving with the

29.text: herd, it is made of the thickest skins with the hair side in, and must be

30.text: renewed every other year, because each bare spot on the surface of the skins

31.text: interferes with the comfort of the inmates. These inner rooms, covered with

32.text: heavy skins, are in use throughout the fall and spring, and among several

33.text: divisions of the tribe — for instance, the people of the Kolyma tundra —

34.text: throughout the whole winter. They are lighted by a single lamp, but heated

35.text: almost exclusively by the animal heat of the dwellers (Plate XIV). Each room
35.note: Roman numeral kept plain ASCII caps (XIV) per keying_spec §2.12, regardless of the small-cap-looking setting; mz draft had it as ‘xIV’.
